newsitem.title: UK: Nickel soars as investment funds buy, shorts cover.
newsitem.headline: Nickel soars as investment funds buy, shorts cover.

text.p: The three months delivery nickel price on the London Metal Exchange (LME) posted impressive gains on Monday on investment fund buying and shortcovering.
Prices at one stage soared to $6,945, the highest level since December 3 and $340 above Friday's close as consecutive buy-stops were triggered.
"Nickel has been the main feature of an otherwise slow LME session," one floor trader said. "The move has been fierce, though I would expect profit-taking to emerge soon," the trader added.
Other traders and analysts agreed saying that the bounce was largely due to a correction from a recent oversold condition.
Scrap material remains in short supply and an expected pick up in demand from the stainless steel industry, which accounts for around 60 percent of nickel offtake, should help to underpin the market.
Also stocks of nickel in LME warehouses have started to fall.
On Friday warehouse stocks fell by a small 12 tonnes, after many weeks of sizeable increases, and several traders expected Tuesday's and upcoming returns to show more substantial declines.
Chartwatchers, looking for clues to future moves from past trends, said the move on Monday has helped to reinforce recent higher pointing chart patterns.
They said a break above stiff resistance at $7,000 could prompt further substantial gains.
LME brokers Rudolf Wolff recently targeted a long term downtrend line around $7,335.
At 1640 GMT three months nickel had drifted back to settle at $6,850/$6,860.
